problem: Suppose $X$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and $det(X)=105.$ The matrix $Y$ is obtained from $X$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{3}↔{R}_{1}$ (switching the first and the third rows). What is the value of $det(Y)?$

activity_context.topic_title: Row and Column Operations on Determinants

feedback.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and $det(A)=-28.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{5}↔{R}_{3}$ (switching the third and the fifth rows). What is the value of $det(B)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since swapping any two rows changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite sign, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =-det(A) \\  & =-(-28) \\  & =28.\end{aligned}
$$
